questions.question: A train has passed at a railroad crossing. What should you do next?

options.text: Wait until the signal lights stop flashing.

questions.explanation: After a train passes, watch for another train on any track. Do not go forward until all gates are up and all warning lights have stopped flashing.

questions.question: Your power steering stops working while you drive. What should you do?

options.text: Honk your horn and turn off the ignition.
Turn on your hazard lights and brace yourself.
Push hard on the steering wheel, slow down, move to a safe area, and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Push hard on the steering wheel, slow down, move to a safe area, and stop.
questions.explanation: When power steering fails, you need more strength to steer. Slow down and move off the road to stop in a safe place.

questions.question: The road is wet or icy. What should you do?
questions.explanation: Wet, snowy, or icy roads reduce your tires' grip. You should slow down when the road is wet or icy.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign shows a divided highway is starting. Stay to the right.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should never:

options.text: Change lanes while inside an intersection.
Check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder.
Check for other drivers moving into the same lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes while inside an intersection.
questions.explanation: Never change lanes in an intersection. Always look over your shoulder to check your blind spot. Watch for other drivers moving into the same lane.

questions.question: Leave extra space in front of your vehicle when following a:
questions.explanation: Motorcycles stop faster than other vehicles. You need extra space to stop if the rider brakes or falls. Motorcycles are hard to see at night because they have only one tail light.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You are entering a one-way street from the wrong direction.
You can go if the road is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are entering a one-way street from the wrong direction.
questions.explanation: If you see these signs, you are going the wrong way and risk a head-on crash. Turn around carefully.

questions.question: What helps someone overcome the effects of alcohol?
questions.explanation: Only time will allow someone to overcome alcohol's effects.

questions.question: Large vehicles have blind spots that can extend 200 feet directly behind them.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles have blind spots that can extend 200 feet behind them. Do not tailgate large vehicles because the driver cannot see you.

questions.question: Backing up your vehicle is:

options.text: Dangerous only if you have a helper.

questions.explanation: Backing up is always dangerous because you cannot see well behind your vehicle. Be extra careful when backing up.

questions.question: When making a right turn on a green light, what must you do?

options.text: Keep driving at your normal speed.
Stop and look for police cars.

questions.explanation: You can turn right or left at a green light unless a sign says not to. When you turn, you must let other vehicles and pedestrians in the intersection go first.

questions.question: What is the best way to avoid a dangerous driving situation?

options.text: Pay attention to everything around your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pay attention to everything around your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Always watch what is happening around your vehicle. Look to the front, sides, and back. This helps you spot problems early and change speed or position if needed.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black symbols on a yellow background. They warn you about hazards ahead. This sign tells you that the divided highway will end soon.

questions.question: What does a red circle with a slash through it on a sign mean?

options.text: Some drivers must yield to others.
Drive slower than the speed limit.

questions.explanation: A red circle with a slash means an action is forbidden. These signs are white rectangles with red and black markings. The symbol shows what is not permitted.

questions.question: A steady yellow traffic light means a ____ light is coming soon.
questions.explanation: A steady yellow light means the red light will appear next.

questions.question: If your tires feel like they lost grip on the road, you should:

options.text: Shift to a lower gear to slow down.
Pump the brakes hard and fast.

questions.explanation: If your tires lose grip, ease off the gas and do not use the brakes. Wait until your tires grip the road again before trying to stop or turn.

questions.question: Double solid yellow lines in the road center mean passing is:
questions.explanation: Double yellow lines mean no one can cross the center line to pass. Passing is not allowed in either direction.

questions.question: On rainy, snowy, or foggy days, use your headlights to:

options.text: Make your vehicle easier for others to see.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make your vehicle easier for others to see.
questions.explanation: In rain, snow, or fog, it is hard for other drivers to see your vehicle. Headlights make you visible. If you need windshield wipers, you must also turn on your low beam headlights.

questions.question: What do work zone signs mean?

options.text: Drive faster to leave the work zone.

questions.explanation: Work zone signs are orange and show that work is happening on or near the road. Be very careful when you see these signs.

questions.question: Where are a truck's blind spots?

options.text: Right next to the cab on the left side.
Both right next to the cab on the left and directly behind the truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both right next to the cab on the left and directly behind the truck.
questions.explanation: Trucks have very large blind spots. The driver cannot see vehicles behind them. If you drive too close behind a truck, you cannot see traffic ahead. If the truck driver cannot see your face in their mirror, they cannot see you.

questions.question: Your blind spot is the area of the road that you cannot see without moving your head.

options.text: You cannot see without moving your head.
You see in your rearview mirror.
You see in your side mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot see without moving your head.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see without moving your head. They are usually on the sides and behind your vehicle.

questions.question: At dawn, dusk, rain, or snow, it is hard to see and be seen. What should you turn on to let other drivers know you are there?
questions.explanation: Turn on your headlights whenever you cannot see other vehicles clearly or when other drivers cannot see you. Use your low beam headlights when bad weather makes you use your windshield wipers.

questions.question: Which statement is true about driving on a wet road?

options.text: As you drive faster, your tires become less effective.
Water does not affect cars with good tires.
Deep water is less dangerous than shallow water.
As you slow down, the road becomes more slippery.

questions.correctAnswerText: As you drive faster, your tires become less effective.
questions.explanation: The faster you drive on a wet road, the less effective your tires are at removing water. If you drive too fast, your tires will lose grip and you will hydroplane, or slide on a layer of water.

questions.question: If a police officer pulls you over, should you immediately get out of your car and walk quickly to the officer's car?
questions.explanation: Stay in your vehicle with both hands visible on the steering wheel when stopped by police.

questions.question: What should you do if your accelerator gets stuck while driving?

options.text: Reach down and pull it up.
Shift to neutral and press the brake firmly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift to neutral and press the brake firmly.
questions.explanation: If your accelerator sticks, keep looking at the road. Shift into neutral and press the brake firmly. When it is safe, pull off the road and turn off the engine.
